domain: AI Governance / Technology Ethics / Risk Assessment
topic_summary: Analysis of the AI risk debate between existential risk (x-risk) and near-term harms framings. The existential risk narrative focuses on speculative catastrophic outcomes from advanced AI systems escaping human control, while the near-term harms narrative prioritizes current demonstrated harms including bias, misinformation, and labor displacement. Both communities claim the 'alignment' label but define it differently: safety as control problem, ethics as justice problem.

key_entities: Existential Risk Community (x-risk advocates: Bostrom, Musk, Open Philanthropy, Future of Life Institute)
Near-Term Harms Community (FATE researchers, digital humanities, AI ethics scholars)
Effective Altruism Movement (funding infrastructure prioritizing tractable high-impact causes including x-risk)
AI Safety Research (adversarial red-teaming, catastrophic failure probing)
AI Ethics Research (sociotechnical audits, bias detection)
Policy Frameworks (White House EO Oct 2023, UK AI Safety Summit)
Bridging Actors (5% of papers accounting for 85% of cross-field links)
key_tensions: Methodological divide: adversarial red-teaming (safety) vs sociotechnical audits (ethics)
Institutional segregation: 80% of collaborations within-community, cross-field exchange depends on handful of brokers
Resource allocation: limited government/multilateral resources split between speculative vs demonstrated harms
Alignment definition: control problem (prevent x-risk) vs justice problem (prevent present harm)
key_claims: Existential risk defined as outcome annihilating Earth-originating intelligent life or permanently curtailing its potential
Near-term harms (bias, misinformation, deepfakes, job displacement) argued more urgent than speculative threats
Distraction hypothesis: x-risk narrative diverts resources from real present dangers
Empirical refutation: respondents more concerned with immediate risks; x-risk narratives increase catastrophic concern WITHOUT diminishing immediate harm concern
Safety-ethics divide is structural not rhetorical: separate conferences, funding, departments, empirical standards
False dichotomy claim: both risk types require integrated approach
key_mechanisms: Funding concentration: Effective Altruism channels tens of billions toward x-risk via Open Philanthropy (Moskovitz/Tuna)
Institutional segregation: 80% within-community collaboration, 5% of papers broker 85% of cross-field links
Policy fragmentation: governance models mirror bifurcation rather than unified human-compatible AI effort
key_absences: Empirical measurement of actual resource diversion (distraction hypothesis tested on public concern, not funding allocation)
Mechanism explaining WHY institutional segregation persists despite thematic overlap and shared 'alignment' goal

axiom_contradictions.basis: Safety reading holds that existential risk is the tractable high-impact cause (effective altruism axiom); ethics reading holds that speculative future harms divert from demonstrated present injustice (precautionary axiom). No single framework can simultaneously hold 'prioritize tractable high-impact future risk' and 'prioritize demonstrated present harm' as foundational without one subordinating the other.

omegas.description: Distraction hypothesis tested on public concern (shows additive not substitutive effect) but NOT on actual funding allocation. The structural claim requires funding flow data absent from research corpus. Is resource diversion a Rope (coordination failure) or Snare (deliberate extraction)?

5% of papers account for 85% of cross-field bridging links. Is this a Piton (atrophied integration capacity) or Scaffold (emerging integration infrastructure)? Removal of small number of brokers sharply increases segregation, suggesting fragility.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) — mechanism explaining WHY segregation persists despite thematic overlap

omegas.description: Are safety_control_reading and ethics_justice_reading genuinely two readings of one kernel, or two distinct kernels sharing a label? Empirical evidence (additive concern, White House dual-track) suggests coherence; institutional evidence (80% within-community collaboration) suggests two kernels. The axiom_contradictions field declares foundational incompatibility, but integrated_reading exists as live position.

Safety_control_reading's victim set (present-day marginalized populations) is observable now; ethics_justice_reading's victim set (future generations) is not. Does this temporal asymmetry make the readings incommensurable, or does it reveal that 'alignment' kernel operates across different time horizons rather than different values?
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) + expected_structural_delta analysis
